title: Chest, heart, abdomen and pelvis anatomy

steps.tx: Thoracic cross-sectional imaging requires detailed segmental bronchial and vascular localization. **Bronchopulmonary segment** anatomy divides the right lung into 10 segments (3 upper, 2 middle, 5 lower lobe) and the left lung into 8 to 10 segments (apicoposterior, anterior, superior/inferior **lingula**, anteromedial basal, lateral basal, posterior basal), bounded by intersegmental veins.

steps.tx: Hepatic cross-sectional anatomy and surgical resection planning depend upon independent vascular supply. **Couinaud hepatic segmentation** is based on independent portal triads (portal vein, hepatic artery, bile duct) into 8 functional segments, where the **middle hepatic vein** separates the right lobe (segments 5 to 8) from the left lobe (segments 2 to 4).

steps.tx: The posterosuperior aspect of the liver exhibits unique hemodynamics. **Caudate lobe** of the liver represents Couinaud segment 1, receiving independent portal venous branches and direct venous drainage into the retrohepatic inferior vena cava, sparing it and leading to compensatory hypertrophy in **Budd-Chiari syndrome**.

steps.tx: Anatomical variation of cardiac arterial distribution determines regional myocardial ischemia patterns. **Coronary artery dominance** is determined by the vessel that gives rise to the **posterior descending artery** (PDA) and posterolateral branch: right coronary dominance occurs in approximately 85% of hearts, left dominance in 10%, and codominance in 5%.
steps.say: Anatomical variation of cardiac arterial distribution is important for clinical practice. Coronary artery dominance is determined by the vessel that gives rise to the posterior descending artery PDA and posterolateral branch, where right coronary dominance occurs in approximately 85 percent of hearts, left dominance in 10 percent, and codominance in 5 percent.

steps.tx: Cross-sectional angiography maps visceral branches of the abdominal aorta and common anatomical variants. **Coeliac trunk** classically trifurcates into the left gastric artery, common hepatic artery, and splenic artery, where **replaced right hepatic artery** from the superior mesenteric artery occurs in 10% to 15% (Michels type 6).

steps.tx: Pancreatobiliary ductal confluence exhibits predictable anatomical drainage arrangements. Pancreatic ductal anatomy demonstrates the main pancreatic **duct of Wirsung** draining via the major duodenal papilla with the common bile duct, whereas the accessory **duct of Santorini** drains via the minor papilla located anterosuperiorly.

steps.tx: Embryological ductal anomalies predispose to recurrent idiopathic pancreatitis in children and adults. **Pancreas divisum** is the most common congenital pancreatic ductal anomaly (5% to 10%), resulting from failure of fusion of dorsal and ventral pancreatic buds such that the bulk of the pancreas drains through the smaller **minor papilla**.

steps.tx: The retroperitoneal spaces are partitioned by multilayered fibroconnective fascial envelopes across the abdomen. Retroperitoneal compartments defined by the renal fascia (**Gerota** and Zuckerkandl) comprise the anterior pararenal space (pancreas, ascending/descending colon, duodenum), **perirenal space** (kidneys, adrenals), and posterior pararenal space (fat only).
